correct_answer: High risk; the executive sponsor departure was never logged in Health Cloud CRM, so the champion-change trigger in the health score methodology never fired, and the CSM hasn't updated the account since February
rationale: The correct answer is B because the decisive failure is process-driven: the champion change (James Whitfield's departure) was only discovered via a Slack thread when Tanya got a bounced email — it was never logged as a contact role change in Health Cloud CRM. Per the health score methodology (SharePoint v3.2 + Brian's own resolved comment), the automatic -15 point adjustment only fires when the CSM updates the contact role. Since Marissa didn't know Whitfield left, she never updated CRM, so the trigger never fired. This compounds with no CSM activity since February, making the 'Forecast Committed' status stale. Answer A is partially correct about over-weighting contract value, but the usage data IS flowing (Pendo shows the drop) — the bigger systemic failure is the champion change gap. Answer C treats the February EBR commitment as still valid despite the sponsor's departure — a classic mistake of trusting stale relationship signals. Answer D is wrong because CSAT-to-CTA automation requires a threshold breach over a rolling window and this is a newer degradation pattern; the real issue is the upstream data gap, not a platform misconfiguration.
